claims.statement: The cluster uses a dual-layer secrets architecture: SOPS + age for Git repository encryption and External Secrets with Bitwarden Connect for runtime secret injection. This separation ensures secrets are encrypted at rest in Git while decrypted values are injected into the cluster at runtime.

SOPS creation rules in .sops.yaml define two encryption patterns: Talos secrets (talos/*.sops.yaml) encrypt the entire file, while Kubernetes and bootstrap secrets ((bootstrap|kubernetes)/*.sops.yaml) encrypt only data and stringData fields using the regex ^(data|stringData)$. Both use mac_only_encrypted: true and a single age recipient.

The age private key for SOPS decryption is stored as a Kubernetes secret named sops-age (kubernetes/components/common/sops/sops-age.sops.yaml), which itself is SOPS-encrypted in Git. Flux Kustomizations reference this secret via decryption.provider.sops and secretRef.name.sops-age.

Bitwarden Connect is deployed via the bitwarden-eso-provider Helm chart (version 1.2.0) and authenticates using the bitwarden-cli Kubernetes secret containing BW_HOST, BW_USERNAME, BW_PASSWORD, and optional BW_CLIENTID/BW_CLIENTSECRET credentials. The HelmRelease configures liveness probes, ServiceMonitor, and CRD installation.

The Bitwarden provider creates two ClusterSecretStore instances: bitwarden-login uses JSONPath login.<property> to access username/password fields, while bitwarden-fields uses JSONPath fields[?(@.name=='<property>')].value to access custom fields on any Bitwarden item type.

The standard ExternalSecret pattern references the bitwarden-login ClusterSecretStore and maps remote Bitwarden item properties (username, password) to local Kubernetes secret keys. Example: tailscale OAuth credentials map client_id from username property and client_secret from password property.

ExternalSecret resources use the target.template.engineVersion: v2 template engine to inject secrets into structured data formats, combining multiple remote secrets with static configuration. Example: Gitea constructs database connection strings mixing secrets (username, password) with static values (host, port, database type).

ExternalSecrets can source different data entries from different ClusterSecretStores within the same resource. Example: growth-tracker pulls username/password from bitwarden-login for Umami credentials, while pulling App Store Connect fields (issuer_id, key_id) from bitwarden-fields.

The bitwarden-fields ClusterSecretStore is required when accessing Bitwarden custom fields rather than login credentials, as bitwarden-login's JSONPath is hardcoded to login.username and login.password only. Example: SMTP relay server's HOST property is stored as a custom field and accessed via bitwarden-fields.

Flux Kustomizations use postBuild.substituteFrom to inject non-sensitive cluster-wide configuration (SECRET_DOMAIN, TIMEZONE) from the cluster-secrets Secret into manifests during reconciliation, enabling environment-specific configuration without per-application secrets.

The mac_only_encrypted: true configuration in .sops.yaml ensures that only fields matching encrypted_regex are encrypted while preserving YAML structure and metadata. This allows SOPS files to coexist with normal Kubernetes resources and maintain git diff readability.

External Secrets Operator reconciles ExternalSecret resources at a configurable interval (default 1 hour per HelmRelease interval). Changes to secrets in Bitwarden are not immediately reflected in the cluster until the next reconciliation cycle.
The External Secrets Operator Helm chart is configured with installCRDs: true, ensuring that ExternalSecret and ClusterSecretStore custom resource definitions are installed and managed by the chart.

ExternalSecret resources can use the sourceRef field to specify different ClusterSecretStores for individual secret keys within the same ExternalSecret, enabling mixed secret sourcing patterns where some keys come from bitwarden-login and others from bitwarden-fields.
